title: Cootie Williams raids Larkin's band in San Antonio
summary: After a fire at the Eldorado, Larkin's band moved to San Antonio where Cootie Williams hired Eddie Vinson and a trombonist but Cobb refused.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And we had Frank Domanian, Eddie Vinson, Vincent, Illinois Jacquet, Jack Kitt, and myself. William Luther Luper was a trombone player, a young boy just come out of Prairie-Prayerview and graduated, and Cootie had come down to catch Milton -- we were under the impression that Milton was, he was the one who told us, that he was gonna take the band and take it to New York, so we had a fire at the Eldorado Ballroom, so we had moved to San Antonio at the Calderman's (UNINTELLIGIBLE) Club there, and Cootie came to San Antonio; he heard the band, but what he did; he come to pick individuals

out of the band. He picked Eddie Vinson Vincent, he picked William Luver Luther, he picked me. Out of the three, I was the only one who refused, so Eddie went, with Cootie Williams. Luver Luther left to go and got on the bus and got to St. Louis, and I don't know what happened; he took sick and died in the hospital. He never got to New York .... trombone player, terrific, never got there. I don't know; it was like tomatoe poisoning, or something like that.

And incidentally, this Monday we had Ellington [Field] playing here, and I'm carrying him on my book of insurance, and I had to strike him because after four weeks, you lapsed him, and I counted four weeks out of my pocket and (unintelligible) man, I can't afford it. And when I get back there, his mother told me his uncle had called, and I called him back and he wanted to know about the insurance, and I said, "I'm awful sorry to tell you that I had to lapse it; I carried it four weeks and four weeks after the four weeks that he didn't pay for it, he just didn't believe in paying for it. He thought he'd live forever; I said, "I don't need no insurance." But I thought I could wake him up; you know, you try when you work together. But he had that -- you know how some kids come right out of college and they think they're smarter than God already, and he was one who thought like that. He's educated now. You know educated in funny kind of ways, doesn't it?
